questionText: Using notes and freehand sketches, discuss the importance of considering each of the following characteristics when designing a house for this site: A A • materials and finishes.

options: When considering what external materials to choose for a new build in a built up area such as this site, consider what materials are already in use on neighbouring building e.g. brick, render, etc
However, more natural materials e.g. timber cladding may also blend into a leafy neighbourhood

If a materials e.g. stone, is readily available in the locality, this would suggest it could be sourced locally and therefore maintain jobs in the area while reducing the carbon footprint or the embodied energy of the build

questionText: Using notes and freehand sketches, discuss the importance of considering each of the following characteristics when designing a house for this site: A A • streetscape.

rows.verbatim: Streetscape

options: It is important to be respectful and mindful of the materials used, the shape and the location of existing buildings along the streetscape
Create a sympathetic building design and additions to fit in with the existing streetscape
Good house design allows individuality without detracting from the character of the street or amenity of neighbours
Creating good streetscape has less to do with individual building design than how the different buildings relate to each other

Consideration should be given to: o House / street boundaries construction and how they relate to the existing o Established building line o Landscaping to enhance the quality of the streetscape – planting, shelter, visual identity o Existing fenestration of the street o Footpath and or cycling lane o Street set-back and house construction line

One approach could be to mimic these characteristics of existing building and therefore aesthetically look similar but also have similar faults e.g. overshadow neighbouring south facing gardens or remove existing nature such as trees
A different approach could be to respond to the individual site while getting inspiration from the existing built environment

questionText: Discuss in detail, using notes and freehand sketches, how each of the following contribute to reducing the transmission of sound in a dwelling house: • completeness.

rows.verbatim: Completeness

options: Completeness is the elimination of all small gaps in the house structure, which increases its airtightness and uniformity

Completeness of the structure depends on airtightness and uniformity: o Blockwork joints to be filled and wall plastered on both sides o Airtight membrane correctly installed throughout the house o Window systems, doors and pipework carefully sealed at external junctions o All window systems and external door designed with double seals installed
High quality craftsmanship required to achieve a more complete (sealed and uniform) structure which will contribute to the overall acoustic properties of the house

questionText: Discuss in detail, using notes and freehand sketches, how each of the following contribute to reducing the transmission of sound in a dwelling house: • flexibility.

rows.verbatim: Flexibility

options: Flexible materials are good at absorbing sound transmissions in a structure

The installation of an absorbent material (quilt, acoustic matting, resilient layer) in a structure will greatly reduce the transmission of sound through that structure: o Quilt insulation between studs in a double stud partition o Quilt insulation between joist in an upper timber floor o Acoustic matting in an upper timber floor

questionText: Discuss in detail, using notes and freehand sketches, how each of the following contribute to reducing the transmission of sound in a dwelling house: • isolation.

rows.verbatim: Isolation

options: As sound energy transmits through the different materials in a structure it decreases – sound level drops
Separating elements of a structure greatly reduces the transmission sound through it

Discontinuing a structural element is effective in reducing sound transmission: o Double / triple glazing when sound travels from glass to gas / vacuum o Separation in walls e.g. double stud partition
Advantage can be taken of isolation to improve sound insulation
